name: Travel_Systems
description: Ship-based travel between star systems, orbital mechanics, and planetary landing.

questions.question: Does travel teach real orbital mechanics and physics?
questions.answer: Yes. Orbital mechanics, gravity wells, fuel efficiency, and celestial navigation are real physics.

questions.question: Can the player learn about celestial navigation through travel?
questions.answer: Yes. Players navigate by star positions, planet orbits, and gravity slingshots. Real astronomy.

questions.question: Does fuel management teach real energy physics?
questions.answer: Yes. Fuel = energy. Different maneuvers cost different delta-v. Real rocket science principles.

questions.question: Can the player learn about gravity wells and escape velocity through gameplay?
questions.answer: Yes. Escaping a gravity well at different altitudes teaches real escape velocity physics.

questions.question: Is space travel visually impressive enough for marketing?
questions.answer: Yes. Space travel screenshots are inherently impressive.

questions.question: Does our travel system differ from other space games?
questions.answer: Our travel teaches real orbital mechanics. Most space games use fake physics for accessibility.

questions.question: Can orbital mechanics be a selling point?
questions.answer: Yes. Teaching real orbital mechanics through gameplay is a unique selling point.

questions.question: Is travel satisfying and educational simultaneously?
questions.answer: Travel must be visually satisfying (cockpit view, stars, planets) and educationally transparent.

questions.question: Do different star systems have different physical properties?
questions.answer: Yes. Different star types, planet masses, orbital distances — real astrophysics.

questions.question: Does travel time feel realistic or tedious?
questions.answer: Travel time must be compressed (fast travel) or engaging (mini-games, education) to avoid tedium.

questions.question: Can the player navigate by visual astronomy?
questions.answer: Yes. Players navigate by real star positions. Different locations show different constellations.

questions.question: Do other ships and traffic exist in space?
questions.answer: Not in v1. Other ships and traffic are future scope.

questions.question: Does travel require the UE5 pipeline to compile?
questions.answer: Partially. The flight component exists. Full travel between systems needs more work.

questions.question: Can basic travel between two points be prototyped quickly?
questions.answer: Yes. Point-to-point travel between two locations can use existing flight component.

questions.question: Does travel require the ship model system?
questions.answer: Yes. The ship model exists in procedural generated content.

questions.question: Can travel be tested via sleepwalker?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can verify travel between points, fuel consumption, and orbital insertion.

questions.question: Does the flight component exist?
questions.answer: Yes. FlightComponent.h/.cpp exists in ProceduralGenerated/Flight/.

questions.question: Does the generator support ship classes?
questions.answer: Yes. The generator creates ship classes with flight components.

questions.question: Is travel data stored in the save system?
questions.answer: Yes. Travel state (position, fuel, destination) can be saved in the save system.

questions.question: Can travel be extended with new destination types?
questions.answer: Yes. New destination types and travel mechanics can be added through the generator.

questions.question: Does this depend on the flight component?
questions.answer: Yes, depends on the flight component and celestial body system.

questions.question: Does this depend on the celestial body system?
questions.answer: Yes, depends on celestial body data (position, mass, orbit) being available.

questions.question: Does this prove the game has exploration depth?
questions.answer: Yes. Proves the game has exploration depth beyond a single planet.

questions.question: Was this derived from Loop 7?
questions.answer: Derived from Loop 7 (Travel) definition.

questions.question: Does travel conflict with the educational scanner focus?
questions.answer: No direct conflict. Travel is a separate gameplay loop from scanning/shelter.

questions.question: What physics simulation knowledge is required?
questions.answer: Basic orbital mechanics and rocket equation understanding helpful. UE5 physics knowledge sufficient.

questions.question: Does space travel serve the most famous educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes. Teaching real orbital mechanics directly serves the educational RPG goal.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by building travel now?
questions.answer: Building travel now means less time on the environmental demo. Tradeoff — demo is marketing, travel is depth.

questions.question: What evidence shows space travel drives wishlists?
questions.answer: Space games with realistic physics (Kerbal Space Program 5M+ copies) prove the market.

questions.question: Does travel chain reach a human learning real physics?
questions.answer: Yes. Player learns real orbital mechanics and celestial navigation through gameplay.

questions.question: Does this work in UE5.8 without hacks or workarounds?
questions.answer: Needs sub-features: flight model, fuel system, navigation, star systems. Major zoom needed.

questions.question: Does this run at 30+ fps on the target GPU (RTX 3060)?
questions.answer: Missing: trade routes, pirate encounters, exploration events.

questions.question: Can a colorblind or hearing-impaired player fully experience this?
questions.answer: Parent (game systems) is designed. No blocker.

questions.question: Does this have sound design that matches the visual quality?
questions.answer: Build after core planet demo. Travel is the second act.

questions.question: Can the community extend or modify this?
questions.answer: Blocked by: celestial body data needs to exist. Blocks: interplanetary gameplay.

questions.question: Can this be translated without breaking?
questions.answer: Star systems, ship types, and travel mechanics can be exposed as moddable data.

questions.question: Does this feature need sub-features, or is it detailed enough at this level?
questions.answer: Needs sub-features at deeper zoom level. Defer until v2 scope.

questions.question: Are there sibling features missing at this level of the tree?
questions.answer: Sub-features exist in the loop board. Create when scoped.

questions.question: Is the parent feature complete enough to support this?
questions.answer: Parent systems are designed at high level. No blocker.

questions.question: Should this be built before or after its siblings?
questions.answer: Build after Environmental_Demo and Educational_Scanner. These are depth features.

questions.question: Does this block other features, or do others block this?
questions.answer: Blocked by animation system (NPC), weather system (Shelter), celestial data (Travel), generator fixes (Tools).

questions.question: Can this feature be verified by sleepwalker beat tests?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can walk through this feature and verify state changes.

questions.question: Does this feature have automated regression tests?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.

questions.question: What are the edge cases and failure modes?
questions.answer: Edge cases include: network interruption, empty state, concurrent access, corrupted data. Documented in threat model.

questions.question: Can this feature be tested in isolation (unit test)?
questions.answer: Partially. Python modules have unit tests. UE5 Blueprint/C++ needs automated test framework.

questions.question: Is there a visual/performance baseline for regression detection?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.
